summary.name: Rancher Desktop
summary.one_liner: Rancher Desktop is an open-source desktop application from SUSE that provides container management and a local Kubernetes environment on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
use_cases: Running containers and Kubernetes locally on a desktop
Testing the impact of Kubernetes upgrades on workloads before production
Building, pulling, and pushing container images during development
Managing local Kubernetes resources through a dashboard
Forwarding ports to Kubernetes services with a click
summary.what_it_does: Rancher Desktop is an open-source app that bundles tools for working with containers and Kubernetes on a desktop. It offers a graphical interface with dashboards for images, containers, and cluster resources, plus CLI and GUI features to build, pull, push, and scan images and run containers. Users can choose the container engine and Kubernetes version, configure networking and registry access, and reset Kubernetes or the container runtime. Bundled CLI tools include docker, nerdctl, kubectl, and helm. On macOS and Linux it runs containerd or Docker and Kubernetes in a virtual machine; on Windows it uses WSL2.
notable: Bundles docker, nerdctl, kubectl, and helm so they need not be installed separately
Uses a VM on macOS and Linux and WSL2 on Windows
Built with Electron and developed as an open source project on GitHub
Choice of container engine (containerd or Docker) and Kubernetes version
caveats: Linux users install through package managers; macOS and Windows use downloadable installers
Resource configuration for the virtual machine applies on macOS and Linux only
